# Lovart

Use this skill when the user asks an AI agent to create or edit visual media through Lovart.

Lovart supports text-to-image, image-to-image, text-to-video, image/frame-to-video, multi-reference video generation, video editing/remixing, background removal, reusable asset upload, and task-result lookup.

Do not use it when the user only wants general creative advice, repo-native SVG/vector/code assets, HTML/CSS/canvas visuals, or edits better handled by an existing design system or local image/video tool.

## Core Rule

The CLI help is the source of truth. Before a real action, inspect the relevant help:

```bash
lovart --help
lovart <command> --help
```

If `lovart` is not installed, use the same commands through:

```bash
npx -y lovart@latest --help
npx -y lovart@latest <command> --help
```

Prefer JSON output when submitting tasks or checking status:

```bash
lovart --json <command> [options]
npx -y lovart@latest --json <command> [options]
```

## What It Can Do

- Generate images from text with `text2image`.
- Generate or edit images from references with `image2image`.
- Generate videos from text with `text2video`.
- Generate videos from first and last image frames with `frames2video`.
- Generate videos from mixed image, video, or audio references with `multiref2video`.
- Edit or remix reference videos with `videoedit`.
- Upload moderated reusable assets with `asset_upload`.
- List uploaded assets with `asset_list`.
- Inspect aggregate asset and replica state with `asset_status`.
- Remove image backgrounds or produce cutouts with `remove_background`.
- List recent tasks with `list_task`.
- Check a submitted task with `query_result`.

## Command Choice

- User wants a new image from a prompt: use `text2image`.
- User wants an image that follows one or more reference images: use `image2image`.
- User wants a new video from a prompt only: use `text2video`.
- User provides first-frame and last-frame guidance: use `frames2video`.
- User provides mixed image/video/audio references for a video: use `multiref2video`.
- User wants to transform an existing video: use `videoedit`.
- User asks to remove a background or make a cutout: use `remove_background`.
- User needs a reusable moderated person/character asset: use `asset_upload`, then use the returned COS URL or `local-asset://...` reference.
- User asks which managed assets exist: use `asset_list`.
- User asks whether one managed asset is ready: use `asset_status`.
- User gives an existing `submit_id`: use `query_result`.
- User asks what has run recently: use `list_task`.

## Agent Workflow

1. Decide the command from the user's goal.
2. Run `lovart <command> --help` or the matching `npx -y lovart@latest` help.
3. Check auth with `lovart auth status` if the command needs account access.
4. If auth is missing, ask the user to run `lovart auth login` or provide a runtime `LOVART_API_TOKEN`.
5. For real submissions, use `--json` and keep the command, arguments, and returned `submit_id`.
6. If the result is unfinished, continue with `query_result`; do not submit the same job again.
7. Stop polling when the task is complete or terminal, then report the artifact URLs or final status.

## Auth Commands

```bash
lovart auth status
lovart auth login
lovart auth logout
```

Non-interactive setup is available when the user explicitly provides a token:

```bash
lovart auth login --token <token>
```

Never print, commit, or summarize full tokens.

## Reference Inputs

Commands may accept public URLs, local file paths, and existing `asset://...` values. Confirm the exact option names with command help.

Common repeated-input patterns:

```bash
lovart image2image --reference ./a.png --reference ./b.png
lovart multiref2video --reference-image ./pose.png --reference-video ./clip.mp4
lovart videoedit --reference-video ./source.mp4
```

When an option is repeatable, pass the option multiple times instead of joining values into one string.

## Submitted Task Results

Treat a generation submit as accepted only when JSON output includes:

- `ok: true`
- a non-empty `submit_id`

Then inspect:

- `done`
- `terminal`
- `next_action`
- `recommended_command`
- `artifact_url`
- `artifacts`

If `done=false`, run the returned `recommended_command` when present, or query directly:

```bash
lovart --json query_result --submit-id <submit_id>
```

If a completed task returns `artifact_url` or `artifacts`, use those URLs directly.

## Model And Option Lookup

Read `references/models.md` only when the user asks which Lovart models, ratios, resolutions, durations, or reference fields are supported, or when you need to validate a user-requested model before submitting.

Still check the command's `--help` before execution, because command help is the live interface contract.

## Good Behavior

- Be clear when you are only reading help versus submitting a real task.
- Prefer one small submission before scaling up to many jobs.
- Do not resubmit unfinished jobs; poll the original `submit_id`.
- Do not expose credentials or saved config details.
- Return the final artifact URL, task id, and status in your answer.
